subject: Staggered renewal: RatingByte hosted commit uplift options
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@ratingbyte.com>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@ratingbyte.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Staggered renewal: RatingByte hosted commit uplift options

Hi Asha / Evan —

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. To keep things simple for procurement while giving RatingByte headroom for the upcoming seasonal burst, I sketched two staggered uplift paths we can take under the hosted plan. High-level options:

1) Phased uplift (recommended)
   - Months 1–3: 2x current monthly committed tokens, existing unit rate
   - Months 4–12: 3x current monthly commit, step-down discounts as volume stabilizes
   - Includes a 30% dedicated burst pocket for the first 90 days (soft-throttle, higher per-token rate)

2) Lump-sum annual uplift
   - Immediate 3x commit for 12 months, 8% annual discount on committed portion
   - Smaller burst pocket (15%) but better overall commit discount

Attached is a short proposal and a rate table with suggested step tiers (Redwood_RatingByte_Uplift_Proposal.pdf).

Questions for you: which path do you prefer from a procurement/timing perspective? If phased looks better, we can draft a staged amendment and a DocuSign for signature and include an explicit ramp calendar.

Next steps: happy to schedule a 30-minute alignment call w/ procurement and engineering this week. Proposed times: Wed 11:00am or Thu 2:00pm PT.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_RatingByte_Uplift_Proposal.pdf (PDF)]

From: Asha Menon <asha@ratingbyte.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@ratingbyte.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered renewal: RatingByte hosted commit uplift options

Logan —

Thanks for the clear options. A few quick clarifying points from our side:

- For the phased uplift, can you confirm how the soft-throttle "burst pocket" behaves? We need to know throttling thresholds and fallback behavior (will requests queue, or degrade to a smaller model?).
- Can you provide the per-token rates for the burst pocket vs committed usage and the applied discounts for months 4–12? The proposal PDF is helpful but we prefer the raw numbers in a spreadsheet for our finance team.
- Procurement (cc Evan) will want the exact billing dates and whether you can split invoice lines by commit vs burst pockets.

We lean toward a phased approach but we need the numbers and the throttling guarantee before we recommend to leadership. If we can get a DocuSign draft and a short Ops SLO note (latency/soft-degrade) we can move quickly.

Cheers,
Asha
Asha Menon
Head of Platform Engineering, RatingByte

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered renewal: Pricing suggestions for RatingByte

Logan —

Copied Karthik for CSM perspective. Two commercial levers I recommend we offer (trade-offs below):

- Early-pay credit: 5–10% credit on committed portion if they prepay 6–12 months upfront. Improves Redwood cashflow, attractive for RatingByte finance.
- Step discount ladder: 0% for months 1–3 uplift, then 6% months 4–6, 10% months 7–12 on committed tokens above baseline.

Ops note: offer a documented fallback that when burst pocket is exhausted, requests fall back to their baseline model variant (same family) with documented tail-latency SLOs. That should address Asha's outage/degrade concerns.

I attached a working rate spreadsheet (rate_table_v2.xlsx). I also suggest we leave a small "on-ramp" credit (one-time) to soften immediate budget impact.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rate_table_v2.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@ratingbyte.com>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@ratingbyte.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered renewal: RatingByte hosted commit uplift options

Hi Asha / Evan —

Thanks — great questions. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

- Burst pocket behavior: when burst pocket capacity is available, requests use the same model paths but are billed at the burst rate (listed in the spreadsheet). If the burst pocket is exhausted, requests continue to be served but are throttled down to baseline commit capacity. For critical traffic we can route to a smaller compatible variant (defined in the Ops SLO doc) to keep p95 latency within 2x of baseline.

- Rates: see rate_table_v2.xlsx for raw per-token numbers (committed unit rate, burst unit rate, and stepped discounts).

- Billing: we can provide separate invoice lines for committed vs burst usage and support monthly invoices aligned to their billing cadence.

Attached: RB_uplift_DocuSign_draft.pdf (draft amendment), and I included the proposal PDF. If this matches your expectations, I can send the DocuSign for signature and loop legal for the PO net-30 terms.

Proposed schedule (if they accept phased uplift):
- LOI / signature on amendment: target by Jun 22
- Implementation kickoff: week of Jun 26 (ops + eng)
- Phase 1 uplift live: Jul 1

Forwarding Kimberly's recommended discount ladder below for transparency:

Let me know which day/time works for a short alignment call — I can hold Wed 11am PT.

Thanks,
Logan
[Attachments: RB_uplift_DocuSign_draft.pdf, Redwood_RatingByte_Uplift_Proposal.pdf]

From: Evan Cho <evan.cho@ratingbyte.com>

Subject: Re: Staggered renewal: RatingByte hosted commit uplift options

Logan / Asha —

Procurement reviewed the draft and we are comfortable moving forward with the phased uplift, subject to:

- Final DocuSign for the staged amendment with the invoice lines split as discussed
- Net-30 payment terms (include PO # when sending the final invoice; PO will be sent after signature)
- One-line confirmation of the burst pocket behavior and fallback (we just need this in the amendment appendix)

Please go ahead and send the DocuSign link and final invoice instructions. We're targeting sign by Jun 24.

Thanks,
Evan Cho
Head of Procurement, RatingByte, Inc.
